To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the resilience perspective provides a useful framework for understanding social ecological system dynamics and that resilience is a key attribute for the sustainability of such systems.

resilience is the capacity of a system to absorb disturbances, and reorganize while undergoing change, so as to still retain essentially the same function, structure, feedbacks, and therefore identity.
social ecological systems are complex, dynamic and adaptive and that the resilience perspective can help to understand the dynamics of social-ecological systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the emergence of a new paradigm for understanding and responding to change in social ecological systems, a paradigm that is increasingly relevant for the management of natural resources and ecosystem services in the face of global change.
the dynamics of social systems, social ecological systems and the interactions across scales.
the emergence of resilience as a perspective for social ecological system analysis, and the implications this perspective has for understanding social ecological systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the resilience perspective is an emergent perspective that is still under construction and will continue to develop as new insights are gained.
the social ecological resilience approach is still in the making and will continue to develop for some time.
resilience thinking is in its infancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
resilience research has evolved to a multi disciplinary science that is now able to address complex social ecological systems in a holistic manner.
we now have a better understanding of the dynamics and the processes that shape social ecological systems, but we are not yet able to predict their behavior.
we have come a long way from the original resilience concept to a resilience perspective for social ecological systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
resilience is not only about the capacity to recover, but also about the capacity to change, to learn, and to adapt.

the resilience approach has the potential of providing a common language across disciplines and sectors and can be used as a tool for understanding, managing and transforming social ecological systems.
resilience thinking is not a theory, but an approach for understanding social ecological system dynamics that is useful for a range of purposes.
